سَنْخَةٌ and ↓ سَنَاخَةٌ A fetid odour: and the latter, [and app. the former also,] dirt; and remains of matter used for tanning. (K, TA.) One says بَيْتٌ لَهُ سَنْخَةٌ (S, TA) and ↓ سَنَاخَةٌ (TA) or ↓ سِنَاخَةٌ (so in three copies of the S) [A tent, or house, or chamber, that has a fetid odour; as is indicated in the S and TA]. And Aboo-Kebeer says, “↓ فَأَتَيْتُ بَيْتًا غَيْرَ بَيْتِ سِنَآخَةٍ
” (so in three copies of the S,) or “↓ فَدَخَلْتُ بَيْتًا غَيْرَ بَيْتِ سَنَآخَةٍ
” (so in the TA,) i. e. [And I came to, or and I entered,] a tent, or house, or chamber, not one of tanning-matter nor of clarified butter. (S.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
